entry.title: Vendster: An Evaluation Arena to Investigate How Forecasting Tool Quality Affects LLM Agent Behaviors in Buyer-Vendor Negotiation
entry.summary:
Time-series forecasters are ranked almost entirely by accuracy metrics, but a forecast's decision value, its effect on the downstream decision, need not track accuracy and is rarely measured. This problem compounds as large language model (LLM) agents increasingly consume forecasters as tools, mediating them through stochastic, opaque policies. We present Vendster, an evaluation arena measuring how a forecaster's bias and prediction-interval width change the outcome of a buyer--vendor discount negotiation between two LLM agents.

Source: arXiv Game Theory, Complex Systems & Soc-Phys (cs.GT, nlin.AO, physics.soc-ph) · Tags: #decision-theory #complex-systems #ml-theory #agents

entry.title: OPERA: OPamp Design by an Expert-Taught Reasoning Agent, from Specifications to Layout
entry.summary:
Analog flows from specifications to a signed-off layout rarely run without manual iteration. Recent large language model (LLM) agents size circuits with optimizer loops over the device dimensions and stop at the schematic. We present OPERA (OPamp design by an Expert-taught Reasoning Agent), in which a general-purpose LLM agent designs CMOS opamps from specifications to post-layout sign-off with open-source tools.

Source: arXiv Systems & Architecture (cs.OS, cs.AR, cs.NI, cs.PF) · Tags: #computer-architecture #kernel-os #ml-theory #agents

entry.title: MinMandate: Task-Hiding Payment Authorization for Web Agents. AI agents increasingly pay for Web services on behalf of their users to complete complex tasks.
entry.summary:
AI agents increasingly pay for Web services on behalf of their users to complete complex tasks. Such a task needs many payments, and the user usually must approve each one, forcing the agent to stop at every payment. Mechanisms such as the Agent Payments Protocol (AP2) therefore enable the user to sign one payment mandate in advance that bounds the agent's payments for the task.

Source: IACR Cryptology ePrint Archive · Tags: #cryptography #zkp #agents

entry.title: Beliefs Over Contracts -- by Francis Annan, Collin B. Raymond. We study how firms choose among incentive contracts and how accurately managers predict their effects.
entry.summary:
We study how firms choose among incentive contracts and how accurately managers predict their effects. Using a survey of managerial beliefs and a large-scale field experiment, we randomly assign agents at the market level to several widely used, expenditure-equivalent incentive schemes. In the field, the best-performing contract raises weekly firm profit by over 55% relative to the status quo, despite being ranked lower by managers, whereas the worst-performing contract performs as predicted.

Source: NBER Working Papers (National Bureau of Economic Research) · Tags: #macroeconomics #econometrics #agents

entry.title: The coupled spread of information and potential-driven motion in evacuating agent populations
entry.summary:
Whether a population evacuates safely depends on two coupled processes: how a warning spreads through it, and how that information moves people. We model this coupling with an agent-based framework, in which each agent's information state--susceptible, exposed, informed or reverted--gates its motion. Only informed agents respond to a global background potential encoding hazards and safe zones, while all agents interact locally through a Lennard-Jones potential.

Source: arXiv Game Theory, Complex Systems & Soc-Phys (cs.GT, nlin.AO, physics.soc-ph) · Tags: #decision-theory #complex-systems #agents
